punchline: Marie Kondo says a shirt you never wore did its job the day you bought it, so you can thank it and let it go.
thirty_sec: Marie Kondo doesn't decide what to keep by price or usefulness. She picks up every single item and checks whether touching it gives a little thrill of joy. If you can't let something go, she says, it's attachment to the past or fear of the future. And for things that fail, she thanks them, because even a shirt you never wore made you happy the day you bought it. Then out it goes.
